synthesis.description: Desk controllers produce the daily position report and P&L for each desk, post the files to shared folders, and answer traders' and managers' questions about moves in the results. Rounds include explaining month-to-date swings, booking prior-period adjustments and liquidations, gathering support documentation for accounting, correcting understated or overstated figures, and restating P&L files. Spreadsheet macros and booklists need refreshing, and system outages delay the report.
steps: The controller runs the desk's positions and P&L from the trading systems.
The P&L file is saved to the shared regional folder and sent to traders and management.
Traders or managers question an unexpected figure or change in month-to-date P&L.
The controller researches the move, checks positions, volumes and liquidation values, and gathers support.
Adjustments or corrections are booked and the P&L is restated where needed.
The explanation and corrected file go back to the requester.
synthesis.approach: Generate each region's P&L and position files on a schedule into a common posting location, with automated checks that flag large day-over-day month-to-date changes and unbooked liquidations, and a standard explanation template listing adjustments with their support.
synthesis.rationale: Much of the effort goes to explaining swings and correcting bookings after the fact; a daily close checklist covering saving to the shared folder, refreshing macros and booklists, checking rolled-off positions and liquidation values catches the recurring errors before traders query them.
